newsitem.title: POLAND: HSBC sees Polish inflation down, GDP up 5.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: HSBC sees Polish inflation down, GDP up 5.5 pct.

text.p: The Polish economy should grow by 5.5 percent this year and five percent in 1998, driven by a combination of investment and private consumption, HSBC James Capel in London said in a report dated April 8.
HSBC said it expected investment to rise 15 percent this year while consumer spending, underpinned by growth in real wages, should rise by six percent.
The report said Poland's deteriorating trade balance was likely to keep the zloty's crawling peg devaluation against a basket of Western currencies at the present rate of one percent a month.

HSBC saw inflation dropping to 16 percent at end-1997 from 17.3 percent in February and consequently real interest rates rising following the central bank's policy of allowing monetary tightening by keeping its official rates unchanged.
Poland's lombard and discount rates are now at 25 percent and 22 percent respectively.
